I am very seriously considering a move to Linux. I have done it before, but always went back to Windows. Microsoft is really beginning to disturb me.

Edit: Ok this is awesome. RDP is available and I have verified that my company offers a Linux version of the VPN client we are required to use. I believe in the next week or so, I am going to commit to a one month hiatus from Windows on my home system.
Is RDP to a windows machine possible from linux?

There's more than one way to do RDP from Linux to Windows. The easiest to set up, and usually free across the board, is for connections on your LAN. If you don't mind the permissions, even Chrome has an RDP. I've used TightVNC, although you may need ssh tunneling.
+1 for remmina. I've been using it since ages for connecting to my client's windows based VPS machines. It's based on GNOME and is much better than the other linux alternatives.

Like it's been said... yes, yes, yes.

Though, so far unmentioned is the client I use regularly - xfreerdp. Comes packages for most distro's, check it out.

You can also solve some "Windows" problems with Wine. It actually works quite well.

Only situations I ever ahve problems with are where there's direct hardware involvement; particularly, automotive OBDC II software like VCDS or INPA. However, they can be made to work in a VM.
